BUG REPORT (from the user): "There is a bug in `errors.go`. Once it is fixed, the test `.::TestErrorUnwrap` should pass; the version of it that checks this is not in the repository, so its name only describes the expected behaviour."

Context: /gin/errors.go defines gin's `Error` type. The in-repo test `TestErrorUnwrap` in /gin/errors_test.go currently exists; the hidden/grading version of that test is NOT in the repository, so you must infer the expected behaviour from the repository's own contracts (doc comments, README, doc.go, existing tests) and from Go's standard-library semantics of errors.Is/errors.As/errors.Unwrap.

Steps:
1. Read /gin/errors.go and /gin/errors_test.go carefully. Note the doc comment on `Unwrap` and on `Error()`.
2. Run `cd /gin && go build ./... && go test -run 'TestError' -v ./...` and record exactly which tests pass/fail. Also run the full `go test ./...` once and save the list of failures (this is the pre-existing baseline).
3. Investigate the git history for clues about the injected bug: `cd /gin && git log --oneline -20`, `git status`, `git diff HEAD`, `git show --stat HEAD`. Report what you find (but do NOT rely on out-of-band knowledge of upstream gin; only on what the repository itself states).
4. Determine the root cause: something in errors.go makes `errors.Is()`/`errors.As()`/`errors.Unwrap()` interoperability not behave as the code's own documentation promises (e.g. a method receiver or return value that is wrong). Consider carefully whether `Error()` and `Unwrap()` method receivers are consistent, and whether a value `Error` vs `*Error` behaves as documented. Write a small throwaway Go test in a scratch dir (NOT in /gin, or delete it afterwards) that exercises `errors.Is(err, innerErr)`, `errors.As(err, &testErr)` and `errors.Unwrap()` for both `Error{...}` values and `&Error{...}` pointers to see which combination fails.
5. Fix the bug in /gin/errors.go with the smallest possible change. Do not add features, do not rename things, do not touch other files unless strictly necessary.
6. Verify: `cd /gin && go build ./... && go test ./...` and confirm that (a) the errors tests pass, and (b) NO test that passed before your change now fails. Compare against the baseline you recorded in step 2.

Report back concisely: the exact root cause, the exact diff you applied (file + lines), the test commands you ran and their results, and any test that changed status (must be none).

Note: you may spawn helper subagents of your own if useful, but you own the final fix and verification.

BUG REPORT (from the user): "There is a bug in `context.go`. Once it is fixed, the test `.::TestContextRenderAndEscapeAttachment` should pass; the version of it that checks this is not in the repository, so its name only describes the expected behaviour."

IMPORTANT CONCURRENCY NOTE: other agents are concurrently editing OTHER files (/gin/tree.go, /gin/response_writer.go) and possibly other regions of /gin/context.go (content negotiation / NegotiateFormat). Do not touch tree.go or response_writer.go. Only edit /gin/context.go and, if strictly necessary, add a small helper in an appropriate existing file; make the smallest possible targeted edit with `edit_file` (never rewrite whole files via shell redirection), and re-read the region right before and right after editing.

Context: /gin/context.go has `FileAttachment(filepath, filename string)` (around line 1039) which sets the `Content-Disposition` header as `attachment; filename="<filename>"` for ASCII filenames and `attachment; filename*=UTF-8''<url.QueryEscape(filename)>` otherwise, then calls `http.ServeFile`. The in-repo tests are /gin/context_test.go (see `TestContextRenderAttachment` and `TestContextRenderUTF8Attachment`); the hidden/grading `TestContextRenderAndEscapeAttachment` is NOT in the repository, so infer the expected behaviour from the repository's own contracts: the doc comments on FileAttachment, /gin/README.md (it documents Content-Disposition and links to MDN's Content-Disposition page, which states that a quoted-string filename must escape `\` and `"`), and standard HTTP header syntax (a `filename="..."` quoted-string cannot contain an unescaped `"` or backslash).

Steps:
1. Read /gin/context.go around FileAttachment, /gin/context_test.go's attachment tests, and the README section about Content-Disposition. Also grep the whole repo for existing helpers that escape quotes (e.g. `escapeQuotes`, `isASCII`, `url.QueryEscape`) and report what exists.
2. Record the pre-existing test baseline: `cd /gin && go build ./... && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -60`; note which tests fail BEFORE your change (some may fail due to other agents' in-flight edits in tree.go/response_writer.go/context.go; record them, do not fix them).
3. `cd /gin && git log --oneline -20 && git status && git diff HEAD` for clues (single initial commit; do not rely on out-of-band knowledge of upstream gin).
4. Determine the root cause and the minimal fix so that a filename containing a double quote (and a backslash) is emitted as a valid quoted-string, e.g. `test"gin.go` -> `attachment; filename="test\"gin.go"`. Note the existing in-repo test `TestContextRenderAttachment` (plain ASCII filename with no quotes) and `TestContextRenderUTF8Attachment` MUST keep passing unchanged. If a helper such as `escapeQuotes` does not exist in the repo, add a small unexported helper (e.g. in /gin/utils.go or /gin/context.go) that escapes `\` and `"`; keep it minimal and idiomatic.
5. Verify with a throwaway test (temp file in /gin that you delete afterwards, or a /tmp module) covering: plain ASCII filename, filename with a double quote, filename with a backslash, and a non-ASCII filename (UTF-8 branch). Then `cd /gin && go build ./... && go test ./...` and confirm no test that passed before your change now fails (compare with the baseline from step 2). Also `go vet ./...` and `gofmt -l context.go`.

Report back concisely: the exact root cause, the exact diff applied (file + lines), the test commands and results, and any test that changed status.

Note: you may spawn helper subagents of your own if useful, but you own the final fix and verification.

BUG REPORT (from the user): "There is a bug in `tree.go`. Once it is fixed, the test `.::TestRouteParamsNotEmpty` should pass; the version of it that checks this is not in the repository, so its name only describes the expected behaviour."

Context: /gin/tree.go implements gin's radix route tree (node types, addRoute, getValue, findCaseInsensitivePath, params handling, wildcards `*` and `:` params). The in-repo tests are /gin/tree_test.go and /gin/routes_test.go; the hidden/grading version of `TestRouteParamsNotEmpty` is NOT in the repository, so infer expected behaviour from the repository's own contracts (doc comments in tree.go, README.md routing docs, existing tests) and from standard HTTP routing semantics.

Steps:
1. Read /gin/tree.go fully, plus /gin/tree_test.go and the routing sections of /gin/README.md and /gin/doc.go. Note the documented semantics of `:param` and `*wildcard` params and of `Context.Params`.
2. Record the pre-existing test baseline: `cd /gin && go build ./... && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -60` and save which tests fail before your change. Also `go test -run 'TestRoute|TestTree' -v .`.
3. Investigate the git history for clues about the injected bug: `cd /gin && git log --oneline -20`, `git status`, `git diff HEAD`. Do not rely on out-of-band knowledge of upstream gin; only on what the repository itself states.
4. Determine the root cause. The test name `TestRouteParamsNotEmpty` suggests that for some registered route, the params extracted for a request are empty (or wrong) when they should not be. Write a throwaway Go test (in /tmp, or delete it afterwards; do NOT add files to /gin) that registers routes with `:param` and `*wildcard` segments (including nested/child groups and cases with a static prefix/suffix around the param) and checks that `c.Param(name)` is non-empty and correct for matching requests. Look for off-by-one/incorrect index arithmetic when computing the param start index, e.g. in `getValue` where it does `value := path[end:]` or `path[valueIndex:]`, or in the handling of `*` wildcard where the leading `/` should be skipped.
5. Fix the bug in /gin/tree.go with the smallest possible change. No new features, no renames, no touching other files unless strictly necessary.
6. Verify: `cd /gin && go build ./... && go test ./...` and confirm no test that passed before now fails (compare with the baseline from step 2). Also run `go vet ./...`.

Report back concisely: the exact root cause, the exact diff applied (file + lines), the test commands and results, and any test that changed status (must be none).

Note: you may spawn helper subagents of your own if useful, but you own the final fix and verification.

IMPORTANT CONCURRENCY NOTE: another agent is concurrently fixing a DIFFERENT bug in the same file /gin/tree.go (about route params extraction in `getValue`). To avoid clobbering each other: (a) re-read /gin/tree.go immediately before making your edit, (b) make the smallest possible targeted edit with `edit_file` (do NOT rewrite the whole file, do NOT use shell redirection to overwrite tree.go), (c) do not touch `getValue`/`addRoute`/param handling unless it is strictly required for YOUR bug, and (d) after editing, re-read the region you changed to confirm the other agent's change is still present.

Context: /gin/tree.go implements gin's radix route tree. Your bug is in `findCaseInsensitivePath` (and its helpers `findCaseInsensitivePathRec`, `shiftNRuneBytes`, `countParams`). The in-repo tests are /gin/tree_test.go; the hidden/grading version of `TestTreeFindCaseInsensitivePathWithMultipleChildrenAndWildcard` is NOT in the repository, so infer the expected behaviour from the repository's own contracts (doc comments in tree.go, README.md, existing tests such as TestTreeFindCaseInsensitivePath / ...WithWildcard / ...WithRedirectTrailingSlash) and from standard semantics: a case-insensitive path lookup must return the correctly-cased registered path plus the extracted params.

Steps:
1. Read /gin/tree.go fully (especially findCaseInsensitivePath and findCaseInsensitivePathRec) and /gin/tree_test.go. Read the routing docs in /gin/README.md.
2. Record the pre-existing test baseline: `cd /gin && go build ./... && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -60`; note which tests fail BEFORE your change (there may be pre-existing failures caused by the other agent's in-flight edit; record them and do not try to fix them). Also `go test -run 'CaseInsensitive' -v .`.
3. `cd /gin && git log --oneline -20 && git status && git diff HEAD` for clues (single initial commit; do not rely on out-of-band knowledge of upstream gin).
4. Determine the root cause. Write a throwaway Go test in /tmp (or a temp file you delete afterwards; do not leave files in /gin) that builds a tree with MULTIPLE children at a node plus a wildcard route, e.g. routes like `/foo/bar`, `/foo/baz`, `/foo/:id`, `/foo/*action` (and variants with several static children and a `*` wildcard), then calls `findCaseInsensitivePath` (via `tree.go`'s unexported API, so put the test in package `gin` in a temp file inside /gin and delete it afterwards, or use the exported router API) with differently-cased paths and checks the returned path and params. Look for wrong index arithmetic when descending into children (e.g. using `i` vs `i+1`/`len(child.path)` vs `len(child.path)-1`), mishandling of the wildcard child (whose path starts with `/` or `*`), or a missing/incorrect `fixTrailingSlash` handling.
5. Fix the bug in /gin/tree.go with the smallest possible change. No new features, no renames, no touching other files unless strictly necessary.
6. Verify: `cd /gin && go build ./... && go test ./...` and confirm no test that passed before your change now fails (compare with the baseline from step 2). Also `go vet ./...` and `gofmt -l tree.go`.

Report back concisely: the exact root cause, the exact diff applied (file + lines), the test commands and results, and any test that changed status.

BUG REPORT (from the user): "There is a bug in `context.go`. Once it is fixed, the test `.::TestContextNegotiationFormat2` should pass; the version of it that checks this is not in the repository, so its name only describes the expected behaviour."

IMPORTANT CONCURRENCY NOTE: other agents are concurrently editing OTHER files (/gin/tree.go, /gin/response_writer.go). Do not touch those files. Only edit /gin/context.go, and only the minimal region needed for your bug.

Context: /gin/context.go contains gin's `Context` type, including `Negotiate`, `NegotiateFormat`, `render.Negotiate`, and the `MIME`/`Accept` handling. The in-repo tests are /gin/context_test.go (see the existing `TestContextNegotiationFormat`); the hidden/grading version of `TestContextNegotiationFormat2` is NOT in the repository, so infer expected behaviour from the repository's own contracts: the doc comments on `Negotiate`/`NegotiateFormat` in context.go, the `render.Negotiate` implementation and its doc comments in /gin/render/render.go, /gin/README.md, and standard HTTP content negotiation semantics (RFC 7231 section 5.3.2: q-values, `*/*` wildcards, ordering by preference).

Steps:
1. Read /gin/context.go (especially Negotiate/NegotiateFormat), /gin/render/render.go (Negotiate + MIME constants), and the existing negotiation tests in /gin/context_test.go and /gin/render/render_test.go. Read the content-negotiation docs in /gin/README.md.
2. Record the pre-existing test baseline: `cd /gin && go build ./... && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -60`; note which tests fail BEFORE your change (some may be failing due to other agents' in-flight edits in tree.go/response_writer.go; record them, do not fix them). Also `go test -run 'Negotiat' -v .` and `go test -run 'Negotiat' -v ./render/`.
3. `cd /gin && git log --oneline -20 && git status && git diff HEAD` for clues (single initial commit; do not rely on out-of-band knowledge of upstream gin).
4. Determine the root cause. Write a throwaway test (a temp file in /gin that you delete afterwards, or a /tmp module) covering: `NegotiateFormat` with a single Accept value, with multiple comma-separated values, with q-values (`text/html;q=0.9,application/json;q=0.8`), with `*/*`, with an empty Accept header, and `Negotiate` with the available MIME types in different orders. Compare the returned format against what the doc comments and RFC 7231 semantics require. Look for wrong loop bounds, wrong index into the split Accept header (e.g. `i` vs `i+1`), incorrect handling of the `,`/`;` separators, or a wrong default when nothing matches.
5. Fix the bug in /gin/context.go with the smallest possible change. No new features, no renames, no touching other files unless strictly necessary.
6. Verify: `cd /gin && go build ./... && go test ./...` and confirm no test that passed before your change now fails (compare with the baseline from step 2). Also `go vet ./...` and `gofmt -l context.go`.
